newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross staffers murdered in their beds in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross staffers murdered in their beds in Chechnya.

text.p: Six Western staff members of the International Committee of the Red Cross, five of them women, were shot dead in their sleep at dawn on Tuesday in the rebel Russian region of Chechnya, the Geneva-based agency said.

Five female medical workers - two Norwegian, one Canadian, one Spanish and one New Zealander -- and a Dutchman were killed in their beds at their residence inside an ICRC hospital compound at 4 a.m., the agency said.
A Swiss staff member of the ICRC, the only surviving witness of the attack, was badly wounded and evacuated, the agency said.

The ICRC suspended work in Chechnya after the killings, the worst ever attack on its staff members. They followed the killing of three of the agency's Swiss workers in an ambush in the war-ravaged central African country of Burundi in June.

"We are under immense shock. These people were murdered. They were killed in their sleep by weapons of war. This is the first time so many ICRC people have been killed in one go," ICRC official Kim Gordon Bates told Reuters in Geneva.
ICRC spokesman Tony Burgener said the agency froze all its activities in Chechnya with immediate effect after the attack.
The six workers were murdered in their residence inside a Red Cross hospital compound at the Novye Atagi village, 17 km (11 miles) southwest of Chechnya's capital Grozny.
Gordon Bates said initial reports said they were shot dead, but later reports spoke of grenades used in the attack as well.
He said ICRC had yet to find out the exact circumstances of the attack.
"What happened is obviously linked to the conflict zone in a very unstable environment," he said.

Both Moscow and Chechnya's separatist leaders are trying to keep the peace settlement on track in the region where tens of thousands of people have been killed in 21 months of fighting between Russian troops and the rebels.
"We are strongly condemning this attack, which is a serious violation of international humanitarian law. The hospital was clearly marked with Red Cross signs all over it," added Burgener.
The remaining 14 Red Cross staff members at Novye Atagi would be evacuated on Tuesday, together with the six bodies, he said.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency quoted Movladi Udugov, first deputy head of the separatist government of Chechnya as saying the incident, if confirmed, "would be a terrible link in a chain of provocations against the fragile peace process in Chechnya."
